title: budget.spent
description: A resource was consumed. One kind covers tokens and CPU alike so budget() is uniform across pools. The substrate REPORTS spend; it does not enforce caps — policy lives in loop config, because caps change far more often than the fact of spending does. Subject is pool:<name>.

pool.description: Which resource pool was drawn from. Current pools: 'claude' (metered, ~17.4M tokens/week on the $20 plan), 'qwen' (local DGX Spark, free but throughput-bound), 'cpu' (the devbox, 16 cores). Free string so pools can be added. A job must draw from exactly one pool — that one-to-one mapping is the whole budget mechanism.

tokens_in.description: Prompt tokens. Zero for non-model work such as the cpu pool. Count UNCACHED and cached together here; record the cached portion separately in tokens_cached.

tokens_out.description: Completion tokens. For the qwen pool this is the real constraint — aggregate output throughput, not context or request count, is what bounds how many lab assistants can run.

tokens_cached.description: Portion of tokens_in served from a prompt cache. Worth tracking: the standing brief is a stable prefix, so with consults inside the cache TTL the fixed context costs roughly a tenth of list price. Big enough to change allocation decisions.

cpu_seconds.description: Core-seconds consumed, for the cpu pool. A full invsqrt verification is roughly 334 core-seconds per seed, so this is the field that reveals whether verification or generation is the real bottleneck.

usd.description: Actual or imputed dollar cost. Null for subscription and local usage. Impute a notional value anyway where you can — it is the only way to compare a free local pool against a metered one.

job.description: Which job type incurred this, e.g. 'propose', 'vary', 'tune', 'verify', 'decide'. Free string: job types are the most volatile part of the system and must never require a schema change.

x-accessors._comment: Which accessor in substrate/accessors.py reads which field IN THIS VERSION. The `resource` accessor returns a normalized Resource for budget(), so adding a new pool dimension (e.g. gpu_seconds) means extending that one accessor, not every caller.
